title: ccp.config.yaml
description: The one file an organisation edits. Everything else in this repository is meant to work unchanged. Created by `ccp init`, checked by `ccp doctor`, and read by every collector. NO CREDENTIALS LIVE HERE - secrets come from environment variables, named in this file but never valued in it, so the config can be committed to your own repository without a secret-scanning incident.

affirming_official.description: The named person who affirms in SPRS. Recorded because the affirmation is a personal attestation with real exposure, not a system action - nothing in this tool ever performs it.

approach.description: The Phase 0 decision everything else follows from. `enclave` isolates CUI to a defined boundary and is the recommended default; `enterprise` puts the whole estate in scope and multiplies assessment cost, control count and SSP surface.

cloud_environment.description: GCC High and DoD tenants do NOT use graph.microsoft.com - they use graph.microsoft.us with a different login host. Getting this wrong is the most common reason a DIB tenant returns 401 against code that works fine in commercial.

break_glass_attribute.description: The user attribute marking a break-glass account. An attribute, never a name pattern: a naming convention is not an access control, and matching on one means the population silently changes when somebody renames an account.

phishing_resistant_methods.description: Which registered methods count as phishing-resistant for this organisation. Configurable because the answer is a policy decision, not a fact.

entity_list_1260h_path.description: A CSV of the current published Section 1260H list. This repository does NOT ship the list - it changes on a recurring cadence and a stale copy is worse than none, because a supplier screened against it reads as screened.

engine.description: duckdb runs locally with no server and no Python, which is what makes this repository runnable on a laptop the day you clone it. The SQL models stay dbt-compatible, so a real warehouse is a migration rather than a rewrite.
